headline: All majors below their 200-day lines with momentum fading; whales pulling ETH and BTC to cold storage while stablecoins flood onto exchanges
paragraphs: The regime is uniformly weak. All seven majors sit below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have printed a golden cross. Bitcoin trades at 63,653, down 0.34 percent on the day and down 1.59 percent over seven days, with price now 49 percent below its 12-month high of 124,773. Ethereum sits at 1,904, off 0.78 percent today, up 1.81 percent for the week but still 60.6 percent underwater from its 12-month peak. Solana, XRP, and Dogecoin are all down on the week and all down more than 60 percent from their yearly highs. Bitcoin dominance stands at 59.1 percent, total market cap at 2.67 trillion, both off 0.42 percent on the day. There is no asset in the sample that holds ground above its long-term trend line, and there is no divergence to suggest a hidden strength underneath.

Momentum tells the same story with one small exception. Bitcoin's RSI-14 reads 47.4, below the 50 midline and well into neutral-to-weak territory. Its MACD has turned below its signal line. Ethereum's RSI sits at 56.3, also sliding, with MACD below signal. Solana, at 42.7, is deeply oversold on the oscillator, yet its MACD remains below signal as well. XRP and ADA both have RSIs in the 42 to 47 range and neither has momentum lift. Only BNB and Doge carry MACD above signal, but BNB's RSI is 48.3 (still neutral) and Doge's is 40.7 (deeply oversold). This is not a picture of momentum breaking the trend. Solana and Doge are deeply oversold by oscillator, which sometimes precedes a rebound, but the MACD configuration says the underlying trend is not accelerating upward. The pair of oversold RSIs without offsetting MACD above signal is worth noting; if they bounce from here, it would be a retest of the downtrend, not a break of it.

Funding and positioning reveal both crowding and fragility, with the fragility tilted toward the long side. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding on OKX is 0.67 basis points, annualizing to 7.4 percent, a modest carry cost. Ethereum's is 1.0 basis points annualizing to 11 percent, more elevated. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is exactly 1.0 (balanced), but Ethereum's is 1.19 longs per short, and the outliers are stark: Solana at 1.9, XRP at 2.11, and Doge at 3.52 longs per short. These are heavily skewed long structures on the altcoins. Over the past 8 to 24 hours, liquidations have favored long positions across the board. Bitcoin saw 1,600 liquidations with 7.28 million in long positions closed versus 5.51 million in shorts. Ethereum saw 1,600 liquidations with 10.8 million in longs versus 4.8 million in shorts. SOL and XRP liquidations over 24 hours showed similar patterns: 5.08 million in longs hit versus 1.54 million in shorts for Solana, and 4.33 million in longs versus 1.75 million in shorts for XRP. The long side is crowded and receiving the liquidation pressure.

Exchange flows present a deeper tension. Over the past 24 hours, whales have moved 110.8 million net off exchanges, a clear accumulation posture, but the composition matters and the weekly trajectory inverts the narrative. Ethereum saw 146 million flow out and completely off the books (no inflows recorded), while Bitcoin saw inflows of 153 million and outflows of 118 million, netting 35 million onto exchanges. The dominant movers off-exchange were Ethereum from Binance (146 million) and Bitcoin from Binance (118 million), both cold storage moves. Yet simultaneously, stablecoins are moving onto exchanges at scale: USDC put 136.5 million onto Binance and USDT added 100 million, together 236.5 million in buying power arriving. The week-level picture is the key counter: the week ending August 3 saw 1.13 billion move off exchanges; the week ending August 10 saw 618 million move back on; August 17 was near flat with 61 million on; and August 24 (the week just closed) saw 802 million flow back onto exchanges. Whales are rotating from accumulation to positioning for sale or hedging. The stablecoin float is essentially flat, up 0.01 percent over 30 days at 308.6 billion, so this is not a new liquidity injection; it is repositioning of dry powder already on the sidelines.

The crowd reads 73 on the Fear and Greed index, solidly in Greed territory. That same crowd has rotated from moving coins to vaults (early August) to dumping coins back onto exchanges (late August). The disconnect between sentiment and the directional flow is instructive: the market is greedy while the people with the largest positions are hedging or lightening. Bitcoin and Ethereum spot ETF flows remain positive, with 5 consecutive days of inflows for both, cumulative year-to-date BTC inflows at 53.8 billion and ETH at 12.2 billion. This institutional bid is real. But it is now facing outflows of native asset by the same whales who moved those assets into the market, a friction that shows up in the week-on-week swing.

Watch the weekly whale flow pattern. If the next week closes with another 500 million-plus flowing back onto exchanges, the accumulation narrative is broken and we are in a distribution cycle masked by strong ETF inflows. Conversely, if Bitcoin reclaims its 200-day line and holds, the technical reset would have to be reconciled with the positioning data, which currently shows the long side as both crowded and under liquidation pressure. Monitor Solana and Doge: their 3.52 and 1.9 long-to-short ratios are extreme, and if funding flips negative (longs paying shorts), that signal would precede a larger long unwind. Bitcoin's MACD cross, currently below signal, is the simplest single condition to track; a flip back above signal with price still below the 200-day would be the first harmonic hint that downtrend was loosening.
